definition: How [[high|high]] or [[low|low]] a sound is. It depends on how fast the air vibrates: fast means high, slow means low.
Higher in [[pitch|pitch]]. On a [[keyboard|keyboard]], high notes are on the right, and on the [[stave|stave]] they sit higher up.
Lower in [[pitch|pitch]]. On a [[keyboard|keyboard]], low notes are on the left, and on the [[stave|stave]] they sit lower down.
A musical instrument, such as a piano, with black and white keys. Each key plays one [[note|note]], and keys on the right sound higher.
The gap between two notes with the same [[note-name|letter name]], such as one C and the next C up. They sound alike, but one is higher.
A sound with a [[pitch|pitch]] and a length, or the symbol that shows it on the [[stave|stave]]. Each note has a [[note-name|letter name]], such as C or D.
The letter that names a note: A, B, C, D, E, F or G. The seven letters repeat as you go up and down the [[keyboard|keyboard]].
The seven [[note-name|note names]] A to G, in order. After G, the alphabet starts again at A.
The C near the middle of the [[keyboard|keyboard]]. On a treble [[stave|stave]] it sits on a short [[ledger-line|ledger line]] just below the bottom line.
The five horizontal [[line|lines]] and four [[space|spaces]] where music is written. [[note|Notes]] sit on the lines or in the spaces.
One of the five horizontal lines of the [[stave|stave]]. A note that sits on a line has its head centred on it.
The gap between two lines of the [[stave|stave]]. A note that sits in a space has its head between two lines.
The pattern of long and short [[note|notes]] in a piece of music, heard over the steady [[pulse|pulse]].
The speed of the music, or how fast the [[beat|beats]] come. It is often written at the start as a number of beats per minute.
